name: Brow-lowering Botox for symmetry

lead: Botulinum toxin (Botox, Dysport) weakens the muscle it is injected into. The frontalis muscle lifts the brows, so relaxing it in one area can let a brow sit lower, which practitioners use to even out brows that sit at different heights.

The appearance payoff is a more balanced upper face. The technique has precedent: Wikipedia cites a 1987 case in which one side of the forehead was injected to match the other side's brow after a facelift left it paralyzed.

paras: Treatment is carried out by trained injectors in a clinic, with small amounts placed in selected forehead muscles and reviewed afterward. Effects appear after several days and last a few months, so the approach is repeated or stopped as the person prefers.
Spread of toxin can affect unintended muscles. Label-listed effects for newer products include drooping of the eyelid and brow, headache and bruising. Effects fade over weeks to months.

angle.text: By weakening part of the forehead's lifting muscle, a clinician can bring one brow down toward the other to balance the upper face.

lead: Brow-lowering Botox is the use of botulinum toxin to reduce the lifting action of the frontalis muscle so that a brow sits lower, often to even out two brows that sit at different heights. Cosmetic toxin is mainly approved for frown lines between the brows (Botox Cosmetic in 2002), with later products approved in 2022 and 2024 [1].

Practitioners also use toxin the other way, to raise the brows, and several registered trials have examined toxin for brow lifting, including studies of Dysport and of toxin's effect on brow height and shape [2][3][4].
Wikipedia records that in 1987 Clark injected the untreated forehead side after a facelift left one side paralyzed, so that the brows matched [1].
infobox: Visible in 3-5 days, peak about a week later [1]

paras: Botulinum toxin blocks signals that make a muscle contract. Smoothing is usually visible three to five days after injection with the maximum effect about a week later, and effects last roughly two to four months [1].
Spread of toxin can weaken unintended muscles; common effects include headache, and the label for letibotulinumtoxinA lists drooping of the eyelid and brow. Bruising can last 7 to 11 days [1].

Registered trials on brow lifting with toxin include a Phase 4 study of Dysport [2], a brow enhancement study [3], and a randomized trial on toxin's impact on brow height and morphology [4]. These test brow elevation rather than lowering for symmetry; no trial specific to brow-lowering for symmetry was found.
